titulo: Questions and indefinite pronouns: Welcher and was für ein

aula.objetivo: Ask questions with welcher/welche/welches, was für ein and wer/wen/wem/wessen, and use the indefinite pronouns man, jemand, niemand, etwas, nichts, alles, alle and viele.

blocos.titulo: Welcher? and Was für ein?, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «welcher, welche, welches» means "WHICH" and picks from known options: «Welcher Pullover gefällt dir?» (Which sweater do you like?). STEP 2: it declines like «der, die, das» and like «dieser»: nominative: welcher Mann, welche Frau, welches Kind, welche Kinder; accusative: welchen Mann, welche Frau, welches Kind, welche Kinder; dative: welchem Mann, welcher Frau, welchem Kind, welchen Kindern. STEP 3: an adjective after it takes the endings it would take after the definite article: «Welchen blauen Pullover?» STEP 4: «was für ein» means "WHAT KIND OF": «Was für ein Film ist das?» (What kind of movie is it?). Here «ein» declines like the indefinite article and «was für» stays fixed: «Was für einen Film möchtest du sehen?» (masculine accusative). STEP 5: for the plural, no article: «Was für Filme magst du?» (What kind of movies do you like?)
blocos.comparacao: English makes the same distinction: "which" (choosing from options) vs "what kind of" (the category). German: «welcher» (which) vs «was für ein» (what kind of). The difference is that «welcher» changes its ending like «der».
